newsitem.title: UK: Two German shipowners form new containership pool.
newsitem.headline: Two German shipowners form new containership pool.

text.p: Two of Germany's leading independent containership owners said they have formed a new operating pool for 15 of their geared containerships.

Reederei 'NORD' Klaus E. Oldendorff Ltd and the Bernhard Schulte Group of Companies said the ships to be included in the O&S Container Pool would be between 1,400 twenty foot equivalent container units (teu) and 1,700 teu.
In a joint statement, the two Hamburg-based firms said the new pool would enable them to serve their customers better.
Because they jointly control a considerable number of modern container vessels, the pool will "offer charterers increased flexibility to meet changing standards," the companies said.
Shipping pools are widely used as a means of increasing market influence and generating economies of scale.
Germany has evolved into the leading source of medium-sized containerships for charter by container shipping lines.
A glut of new shipbuilding in recent years stimulated by German tax breaks for shipping investors, has caused charter rates to fall sharply, however.
Industry analysts claim there appears little prospect of rates recovering in the short term.
The core of the new pool will be the B-186 type series of vessels built at the Szczecin shipyard, the two companies said. It gave no further details.
Dr Bernhard Schulte declined to comment. --Reuters Shipping Desk +44 171 542 4087/4012. Fax 542 5017.
